input.text: Look closely at the loop in main.py that walks through the list of numbers. The range it uses begins at one, so it starts with the second number and never visits the first number.

content.text: The issue is in that loop's starting range: it begins at one instead of zero, skipping the first list element.

input.text: In Python, list indexes start at zero. Your loop's range starts at one, so it treats the second item as the first one and never adds the actual first item. If you make the range begin at zero, the loop will visit every number in the list and the total will be correct.

content.text: That loop needs to start at index zero, because Python lists are zero-indexed. Starting at one skips the first number entirely, which is why the sums are too small.
